red_flag_claims.claim_text: Serve generated $2.7 million in revenue for FY2025 (vs $1.8M in FY2024) against a net loss of $101.4 million and accumulated deficit of $208.9 million.
supports: Direct disclosure in 10-K MD&A. Revenue $2.65M, cost of revenue $18.0M (gross loss $15.4M — i.e. gross margin of NEGATIVE 580%), opex $97.4M, net loss $101.4M.
Cash burn from ops $80.2M in FY2025 alone, accumulated deficit $208.9M.
Subsequent capital raises: $80M (Jan 2025) and $100M (Oct 2025), plus stock-funded M&A — clear distress-adjacent funding cadence.
red_flag_claims.M_check: Internal financials only — no external M-source needed for arithmetic. The headline is staggering: gross margin is negative 580% (cost to provide $1 of delivery service is $6.80). Combined with the disclosed material weaknesses in ICFR (see C5), this is a Heuristic 10 distress fingerprint.
red_flag_claims.interpretation: Heuristic 10 + Heuristic 11. The company is generating $2.7M of revenue against $101M of annual losses (revenue is 2.6% of losses), with deeply-negative gross margins indicating the unit economics of robotic delivery do NOT work at current scale. Note the company's three acquisitions (Voysys Apr-25, Vayu Aug-25, Diligent Jan-26, Vebu Feb-26) and capital raises are stretching capital ahead of any commercial-revenue inflection. Scored RED because (a) gross margin is negative-multiple-hundred-percent and (b) growth pattern is acquisitive-cash-burning with no demonstrated unit economics at scale, not a Heuristic 4 'investment-led equity round' that comes with a customer commitment.

red_flag_claims.claim_text: Management concluded disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting were not effective as of Dec 31, 2025 due to multiple material weaknesses (segregation of duties, control environment, comprehensive accounts and disclosures).
supports: Item 9A of the 10-K explicitly states 'our principal executive officer and principal financial officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective.' Multiple distinct material weaknesses enumerated (control environment, segregation of duties, controls over substantially all accounts and disclosures).
Acknowledgement of 'comprehensive' deficiencies covering essentially all financial reporting areas.
red_flag_claims.M_check: Self-disclosure. This is a serious, broad, multi-area failure — not a narrow technical material weakness. It explicitly admits the company lacks the size/resources for effective controls. Particularly notable given the company completed FOUR acquisitions (Voysys, Vayu, Diligent, Vebu) in a 10-month window across 2025–early 2026, each requiring complex purchase-price allocation, and acknowledges that Diligent and Vebu accounting is incomplete at filing.

weaknesses_disclosed: controls over substantially all accounts and disclosures

red_flag_claims.interpretation: Broad-scope material weakness in a company actively executing serial M&A is a Heuristic 10 distress fingerprint and elevates the reliability risk of all other financial claims in this filing (including the customer concentration table and revenue disclosure). Scored RED because the weaknesses are not narrow / remediated — they cover 'substantially all accounts and disclosures' which is essentially a blanket admission.

severe_claims.claim_text: Serve maintains platform-level integrations with food delivery platforms, such as Uber Eats and DoorDash, that enable real-time order dispatch and operational coordination.
supports: edgar_fts cik=Uber (0001543151) search 'Serve Robotics': total_hits=1 — a single Q4-2021 earnings press-release 8-K (2022-02-09). NO mention in any Uber 10-K, 10-Q, or DEF 14A through cutoff.
edgar_fts cik=Uber search 'sidewalk delivery': total_hits=0.
edgar_fts cik=DoorDash (0001792789) search 'Serve Robotics': total_hits=0.
severe_claims.M_check: Counterparty-disclosure cross-check per Layer 3 Rule 7. Uber Eats is positioned as the centerpiece partnership and counts for the majority of revenue via Customer A (37%) / Customer B (18%) profile, but the counterparty has effectively zero disclosure footprint.
severe_claims.interpretation: Hard counterparty-asymmetry signal. Uber's 10-K does not name Serve as a material partner/customer at any point — only a 2022 earnings-press-release tag-out. For Uber, the Serve relationship is immaterial (which is consistent with Uber's scale — ~$45B revenue), but on the SERV side this relationship is the entire business thesis. Heuristic 7 says ABSENCE for a pilot-stage relationship = MODERATE; ABSENCE while company claims headline customer revenue = RED. Here SERV concentrates 37% of revenue in 'Customer A' (most plausibly Uber Eats) — that IS headline customer revenue. Rating SEVERE rather than RED because Uber's scale legitimately excuses non-disclosure (Serve is too small to be material to Uber) — but the asymmetry still indicates the relationship has not graduated past pilot/limited-deployment status, contradicting the framing in SERV's filing.

moderate_claims.claim_text: As of December 31, 2025, Serve's fleet consisted of over 2,000 sidewalk delivery robots.
supports: uspto_odp.query_assignee returned 7 applications / 2 granted patents for 'Serve Robotics', including DELIVERY ROBOT and SELF SANITIZING STORAGE OF A DELIVERY ROBOT — consistent with a real delivery-robot R&D effort, but the patent footprint is small relative to a 2,000-unit claim.
moderate_claims.M_check: uspto_odp.query_assignee: n_granted=2, n_total_applications=7; category 'robot' hits=4. Filing also discloses FY2025 revenue of only $2.7M against the 2,000-robot fleet claim — ARPU per robot ~$1,350/year, which implies very low utilization vs the headline fleet number. No M-source directly counts deployed sidewalk robots.
moderate_claims.interpretation: STAGE LADDER applied (Heuristic 3). Headline 'over 2,000 robots' is a fleet/inventory figure not a commercial-deployment figure. $2.7M revenue across 2,000+ robots = ~$1,350/robot/year — clearly inconsistent with commercial utilization. Either fleet is heavily idle / inventory-staged, or many robots are not yet revenue-producing. Pilot-vs-commercial conflation per Heuristic 9. Scored MODERATE because the fleet number itself is plausible (filing-stated) but is being marketed as an operational figure when revenue per robot betrays minimal utilization.

moderate_claims.claim_text: For FY2025, Customer A represented 37% and Customer B represented 18% of total revenues; combined ~55% from two unnamed customers (likely Uber Eats and DoorDash).
supports: Customer concentration disclosed in SERV's own 10-K (Customer A 37%, Customer B 18% in 2025; Customer A 26%, Customer B 65% in 2024) — note dramatic shift: Customer B went from 65% to 18% — a >70% YoY decline in proportional revenue from that customer, while total revenue grew only 46%. Implies Customer B revenue declined meaningfully in absolute terms.
Neither customer is named in the 10-K (Heuristic 9: name-variant fragility but here the company itself withholds the name).
Counterparty disclosure on Uber side = single 2022 8-K only; DoorDash side = zero.
moderate_claims.M_check: Cross-checked SERV's own 10-K disclosure against Uber/DoorDash counterparty filings via edgar_fts. SERV chose Customer A/B/C/D/E pseudonymization rather than naming the counterparty, despite the partner relationship being central to the equity story.
moderate_claims.interpretation: Two concerning sub-signals: (1) Customer B's share collapsed from 65% to 18% YoY — and since total revenue only grew 46% ($1.8M → $2.7M), Customer B's absolute revenue dropped from ~$1.18M to ~$0.48M, a ~60% decline. That looks like a major customer churn or pilot wind-down. (2) Refusal to name partners despite marketing the Uber Eats / DoorDash relationships in MD&A and risk factors is a soft-but-real red flag. Scored MODERATE because the disclosure is technically compliant and the customer churn is acknowledged via the customer-concentration table itself.

moderate_claims.claim_text: On January 27, 2026 Serve completed the acquisition of Diligent Robotics Inc. (Moxi healthcare robots) for ~$29M, extending the platform to hospitals and citing 'established commercial relationships with healthcare systems and institutions.'
supports: uspto_odp shows Diligent Robotics has 6 granted patents and 23 total applications, all in robotic learning / navigation / manipulation / multi-sensor perception domains (category 'autonomy' hits=21). The IP is real and tech-relevant to indoor hospital robotics.

However, the 10-K does not name ANY healthcare-system customer of Diligent (no specific hospital networks, no Joint Commission certifications named, no contract values disclosed), and the 'established commercial relationships' claim is presented as a forward-looking expectation rather than a current revenue figure.
Acquisition accounting is explicitly 'incomplete' at 10-K filing date — Serve has not yet assigned purchase-price values.
moderate_claims.M_check: USPTO confirmed Diligent's IP depth (Heuristic 8 PASS-equivalent on patents). Counterparty-disclosure check NOT performed because no specific health-system customers are named (no anchor to look up). The cohort prompt warns 'pilots-as-PR is the central evasion pattern' — the 'established commercial relationships with healthcare systems and institutions' language is exactly the kind of qualitative, unverifiable claim that Heuristic 9 flags.
moderate_claims.interpretation: Patent footprint validates Diligent's technology bona-fides. The 'established commercial relationships' phrasing without naming any specific health system or disclosing the inherited revenue base earns a MODERATE rating. The fact that the acquisition closed only ~6 weeks before 10-K filing and PPA is incomplete prevents a more aggressive call but also prevents the company from substantiating the 'scalable, recurring revenue growth' narrative — Heuristic 3 stage ladder is clearly being skipped. The pivot from sidewalk delivery to a second vertical (healthcare) plus a third (Vebu food tech) within months is a classic 'shopping for a thesis' pattern when the core business is not scaling.

red_flag_claims.claim_text: Going concern: $227.0M accumulated deficit, $33.8M net loss, $30.3M cash used in operating activities for FY2025; auditor issued substantial-doubt going-concern qualifier.
red_flag_claims.supports: BPM LLP explicit going-concern paragraph ("raise substantial doubt about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern"). Q1 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-05-15) reconfirms substantial doubt: cash dropped from $20.6M (YE2025) to $11.4M (Mar 31 2026), with Q1 op cash burn $11.6M. At that burn rate, runway without additional financing is under 3 quarters.
red_flag_claims.interpretation: Going-concern qualifier is explicit and reaffirmed in Q1 2026. Cash burn accelerated QoQ (from ~$7.6M/quarter FY2025 avg to $11.6M in Q1 2026, partly due to KSF acquisition cash outflow of $6.1M). Company is structurally dependent on ATM equity issuance — see C8.

red_flag_claims.claim_text: Total order backlog of approximately $3.1M as of March 24, 2026 ($0.6M ASR + $2.5M ECD).
red_flag_claims.supports: Self-disclosed backlog in 10-K Risk Factors. $0.6M of ASR backlog is the binding signal: ASR (the autonomous-robot core product) has under $1M of forward orders against $33.8M annual operating loss. Backlog is 27% of FY2025 revenue and falling vs. company narrative of commercial scaling.
red_flag_claims.M_check: internal_disclosure + cross-check via Q1 2026 10-Q (no backlog uplift disclosed)
red_flag_claims.interpretation: Tiny $0.6M ASR backlog is direct quantitative contradiction of the 'building the nation's first Autonomous Security Force' positioning. With ASR depreciation alone at $2.0M/yr and ASR-related service revenue ~$8.0M total, $0.6M of new ASR orders implies the install-base lift is decelerating. Combined with the going-concern overhang, this is a HARD signal of forward-revenue weakness in the core platform.

red_flag_claims.claim_text: ATM offering program produced $42.8M FY2025 + $9.0M Q1 2026 + $3.3M April-May 8 2026 ($55M+ net in 16 months); $18.3M remaining on shelf at May 8 2026. Class A shares grew from 4.07M (YE2024) to 12.19M (YE2025) and ~14.9M+ post Event Risk issuance.
red_flag_claims.supports: Self-disclosed in 10-K MD&A and Q1 2026 10-Q Subsequent Events. Magnitudes verifiable in cash flow statement ($42.2M FY2025 financing inflow). Share count trajectory in equity rollforward.
red_flag_claims.interpretation: ~3.7x share-count expansion in 15 months funded almost entirely by ATM dilution — this IS the going-concern remediation. Combined with multiple historical reverse-splits (per cohort metadata and the 'fractional share adjustment due to reverse stock split' line in FY2024 equity rollforward), the structural dependence on ATM issuance against a declining ASR backlog is a classic distress fingerprint per Calibration 10. Listed price reference ($10.00 Nov-2024 offering) implies ATM issuance well above $10/share now, but each issuance is highly dilutive given the low share count base.

moderate_claims.claim_text: One client = 19% of FY2025 revenue (zero such clients in 2024); two clients = 28% and 11% of AR at YE2025.
moderate_claims.supports: 10-K Note on Concentrations of Credit Risk discloses customer concentration. The CLIENT IS NOT NAMED in the filing. Per Layer 3 Rule 7, an unnamed 19% customer prevents counterparty cross-check; we cannot verify in any counterparty 10-K. EDGAR FTS shows zero non-KSCP filers reference 'Knightscope' in 10-K results, but absence is expected for a $2.2M annual revenue contribution (well below any counterparty's materiality threshold).
moderate_claims.interpretation: Per Calibration 7, absence of counterparty disclosure for a $2M customer is NOT a hard contradiction — too immaterial to trigger 10-K mention on the customer side. Score MODERATE because the named-customer transparency is missing and the new concentration risk (zero to 19% YoY) suggests a single-deal lift rather than broad commercial scaling.

moderate_claims.claim_text: K7 ASR remains in development; commercial production not expected until late 2026 or early 2027; K7 contributed zero revenue in 2025.
moderate_claims.supports: 10-K MD&A explicitly states K7 contributed zero revenue in 2025 and that commercial production targets late-2026/early-2027 'subject to development milestones and supply chain readiness'. USPTO confirms 11 granted patents — robotics IP exists (see C7).
moderate_claims.interpretation: Per Calibration 3 (planned vs operational): K7 is still at pre-commercial stage. The repeated push of commercial production timeline (now 'late 2026 or early 2027') is a soft-deferral pattern consistent with pilots-as-PR risk. Not a hard fabrication — the company is transparent that K7 has $0 revenue. Score MODERATE: company is honest about the gap but the new-platform optionality is being relied on to justify the R&D spike (R&D +77% YoY to $12.5M, 110% of revenue).

moderate_claims.claim_text: Acquired Event Risk LLC (KSF) on Feb 27, 2026 for ~$18M total consideration; recorded $7.7M goodwill + $15.5M customer-relationships intangible.
moderate_claims.supports: EDGAR FTS confirms the deal: 9 KSCP filings reference 'Event Risk' (8-K 2026-03-03, 8-K/A 2026-05-15 with Reg S-X financials, 10-K 2026-03-27, 10-Q 2026-05-15). Counterparty (Event Risk LLC) is a private Indiana LLC so no SEC corroboration is possible — by construction.
moderate_claims.interpretation: Acquisition is verified via 8-K/A with full Reg S-X financial statements (filed 2026-05-15). However, two cautions per Calibration 4: (a) for a $30M-burn microcap with going-concern qualifier to pay ~$11M cash+debt-repay+deferred (plus shares) for a security-guarding services business is a pivot away from the autonomous-robot pure-play, with $15.5M of intangibles (customer relationships) representing ~86% of purchase price — high reliance on retention of acquired customer book. Score MODERATE: real transaction but quality / strategic-fit risk is elevated.

moderate_claims.claim_text: Knightscope serves government clients (per cohort metadata, municipal/private-security customers).
moderate_claims.supports: USAspending returns 5 federal contract awards 2020-2026 totaling only $241,512: VA ($88.8K, $36.4K), DoD/Air Force ($73.4K, $23.4K), DoI ($19.6K). Descriptions are dominated by 'EMERGENCY CALL BOX SYSTEM', 'AUTONOMOUS PUBLIC SAFETY SOLUTIONS FOR US AIR FORCE INSTALLATION SECURITY NEEDS', and call-box repairs. Total federal contract dollars over 5+ years = ~2.1% of FY2025 revenue alone.
moderate_claims.interpretation: Per Calibration 5 + 7: USAspending captures federal contracts. There IS one DoD/Air Force ASR contract ($73K — directly on-mission), which validates the existence of federal ASR pilot activity — score is NOT RED. However, $241K cumulative over 5+ years vs. company emphasis on 'government' as a market segment shows federal channel is sub-material. Municipal/private-security customers (the bulk of the cohort metadata's named segment) would not appear in USAspending; this is a true UNVERIFIABLE for municipal, but the federal slice is verifiably tiny. Score MODERATE: claim is technically true but quantitatively trivial relative to positioning.

severe_claims.claim_text: $248M total backlog at 12/31/25; $27M attributable to 10%+-customers; only $8.2M of Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO).
severe_claims.supports: The 30x gap between '$248M total backlog' (non-GAAP, includes Unfunded Backlog + Priced Unexercised Options + Unpriced Unexercised Options per BBAI's own definitions) and the ASC 606 GAAP RPO of $8.2M is extreme. Only $8.2M is contractually firm (signed sales orders); the remainder depends on funding appropriations, option exercises, and unpriced option execution. Even within the $248M, only $27M is from the customers driving 51% of revenue and expected to recognize within 2026. Risk-factor language explicitly warns: 'the contracts comprising our backlog may not result in actual revenue in any particular period or at all.'
severe_claims.M_check: filing-internal cross-check (RPO $8.2M vs backlog $248M); usaspending verification of prime relationships
severe_claims.M_value: Total backlog $248M vs ASC 606 RPO $8.2M (~30x gap)
severe_claims.interpretation: Backlog disclosure conflates ceiling/option value with firm contract value. This is the defense-services analog of Calibration Heuristic 9 (pilot-vs-deployment conflation): unfunded/optioned backlog presented as commercial visibility. The $8.2M RPO is the only number bound by GAAP. SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY of the backlog narrative — headline overstates near-term contracted revenue by an order of magnitude.

moderate_claims.claim_text: FY2025 revenue $127.7M; US gov 90% ($114.7M); 10%+-concentration customers = $65M (51% of revenue).
moderate_claims.supports: Direct USAspending lookup of BigBear.ai Federal LLC returned only 8 awards totaling $15.3M lifetime ($7M EXIM-Bank, $8.3M DoD). Direct DoD-prime contracts are far below the $114.7M FY25 US government revenue claim, implying the vast majority is earned as SUBCONTRACTOR work to prime integrators — typical pattern for cleared mid-cap defense services. Acquired entities ProModel ($35M lifetime, 30 awards) and NuWave ($12M lifetime, 8 awards) account for additional direct prime revenue. Revenue DECLINED 19.3% YoY ($158.2M -> $127.7M) despite narrative of 'strongest financial position in history.' Air Force EPASS wound down. Single-customer A/R of $3.4M >10% (new concentration in FY25, not present in FY24).
moderate_claims.M_value: BigBear.ai Federal LLC: 8 awards, $15.3M lifetime; ProModel: 30 awards $35M; NuWave: 8 awards $12M
moderate_claims.interpretation: US government revenue claim is plausible only with heavy subcontract intermediation. Year-over-year revenue decline of ~20%, combined with single-customer A/R >10% concentration and material $65M=51% revenue concentration in 10%+ customers, plus EPASS wind-down — supports MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY of the upbeat narrative. Not a hard contradiction (subcontract pattern is real), but the marketing-vs-reality gap is material.

moderate_claims.claim_text: BigBear.ai holds patent IP across AI, computer vision, predictive analytics, biometrics, perception, orchestration and digital identity.
moderate_claims.supports: uspto_odp.query_assignee returned 0 granted patents for 'BigBear', 0 for 'Pangiam' (the recently-acquired biometrics/digital-identity subsidiary that was the IP cornerstone of the digital-identity narrative), 0 for 'ProModel', 0 for 'Ask Sage', and 0 for 'Open Solutions'. The one acquired entity with material patents is NuWave (44 granted), and Analex (2 granted, may not be BBAI's Analex). The biometrics/computer-vision/orchestration tech areas the 10-K markets most heavily have no granted-patent footprint under USPTO assignee search.
moderate_claims.M_check: uspto_odp.query_assignee for BigBear / Pangiam / Ask Sage / subs
moderate_claims.M_value: n_granted: BigBear=0, Pangiam=0, Ask Sage=0, ProModel=0, NuWave=44
moderate_claims.interpretation: Filing language is careful ('not dependent on any particular patent or application'), which is consistent with the absence of a BBAI-branded patent footprint. The biometrics-and-digital-identity narrative (acquired via Pangiam for biometric/digital-identity tech) is not supported by Pangiam having granted patents under that name. Calibration Heuristic 8 applies in reverse: BBAI sells SERVICES + software, not patentable hardware. The patent claim is soft to begin with, but the marketed 'forefront of technological advancement' framing of biometrics/digital-identity vs zero Pangiam-branded patents = MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY of the tech-leadership narrative.

moderate_claims.claim_text: $461.5M total liquidity at 12/31/25; debt reduced from $200.8M to $17.7M subsequent to year-end (88% reduction). 'Strongest financial position in history.'
moderate_claims.supports: Cross-check is filing-internal (no external M-source needed for the dollar figures themselves). The $461.5M liquidity number is real BUT was achieved by selling 142,253,313 shares under three ATM agreements in FY2025 alone for $637M gross. Common stock outstanding ballooned from 251,554,378 (12/31/24) to 436,955,655 (12/31/25), a 73.7% one-year share-count increase. Debt reduction was achieved primarily by CONVERSION of 2029 Convertible Notes into common stock (38.1M shares issued in Jan 2026), not by cash repayment. Combined dilution YoY is well over 90% when including the convert-driven shares. Restructuring charges of $4.37M in FY25 (vs $1.29M in FY24) indicate ongoing organizational disruption.
moderate_claims.M_check: filing-internal: share count, ATM proceeds, convert mechanics, restructuring activity
moderate_claims.M_value: shares: 251.5M -> 436.9M (+73.7%); ATM gross $637M FY25; 2029 notes converted to 38.1M shares Jan 2026; restructuring $4.37M FY25
moderate_claims.interpretation: Liquidity is real but bought at extreme dilution + convert-into-equity rather than retire-with-cash. Calibration Heuristic 10 applies (distress fingerprints): three back-to-back ATMs in one year, mass convert-to-equity, growing restructuring charges. The 'strongest in history' framing of capital structure ignores that capital-raising came from share issuance, not cash generation. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY of the balance-sheet-strength narrative.

moderate_claims.claim_text: Pangiam acquisition (Feb 2024) brought biometric/digital identity capabilities; Air Force EPASS wound down Q2 2023; cost of revenues rose to 78% in FY25 (vs 71% in FY24).
moderate_claims.supports: usaspending recipient='Pangiam' returned 0 federal awards 2020-2026 — the biometric/digital-identity acquisition has no detectable direct federal contract revenue under its own name. Cost of revenues at 78% of revenue (FY25) leaves only ~22% gross margin, far below typical defense-software multiples. Air Force EPASS wind-down (Q2 2023) was confirmed as a material revenue drag in FY24 vs FY23, and that drag has not been offset by new program wins large enough to keep total revenue flat (FY25 is down 19% YoY).
moderate_claims.M_value: Pangiam direct awards=0; cost of rev: FY25=78%, FY24=71%, FY23=74%
moderate_claims.interpretation: Pangiam's biometrics capability does not appear as a federal-prime revenue line. Either it is also subcontracted (typical for cleared biometrics work to CBP/TSA via primes) or commercial in nature. Combined with margin compression and EPASS wind-down, the 'transformation' narrative is moderate-underdelivery. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY.

severe_claims.claim_text: Material weakness in ICFR re cost-of-revenue timing (FY25, adverse Grant Thornton opinion) + prior FY24 material weakness on revenue recognition (remediated FY25) + pending securities class actions (Decker/Traina) alleging false statements on rev rec, deployment times, internal controls
supports: sym_19_self_disclosure_hits_for_material_weakness
active_securities_class_actions
severe_claims.M_value: 19 hits in SYM's own filings for 'material weakness'. Two consecutive fiscal years (FY24, FY25) of material-weakness disclosure. FY24 weakness was on revenue recognition (cost overruns not billable) — directly on the revenue line. FY25 weakness shifted to cost-of-revenue timing — which under percentage-of-completion accounting ALSO impacts revenue recognition. Grant Thornton (independent auditor) issued an adverse opinion on ICFR for FY25. Two putative securities class actions (Fox dismissed; Decker → amended as Traina) pending; Traina specifically alleges misstatements on 'revenue recognition, deployment times, and internal controls' for the Feb 2024-Feb 2025 class period; motion to dismiss hearing was scheduled for Dec 16, 2025.
severe_claims.interpretation: SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY. Per Heuristic 11 (revenue-recognition pattern, robotics-specific) and Heuristic 9 (pilot vs deployment conflation tied to deployment-time misstatement allegations in the class action), this is the central forensic-disclosure concern. The framework should treat any forward-revenue or backlog-conversion claim by SYM with elevated skepticism while (a) the adverse ICFR opinion remains outstanding, (b) the second consecutive material-weakness disclosure is unremediated, and (c) the Traina securities class action is unresolved. Note: the FY25 weakness is self-characterized as 'immaterial' in actual misstatement terms — but the persistence of weakness across two cycles, with auditor adverse opinion, is itself the red flag.

moderate_claims.claim_text: Jan 2025 ASR acquisition from Walmart + 2025 Walmart MAA: 400 micro-fulfillment system commitment, $520M dev funding to SYM
supports: walmart_2025_2026_earnings_mentions
moderate_claims.M_value: Walmart's 8-K earnings presentations in 2025 and 2026 (5 filings post-deal close) continue to mention Symbotic, but neither 'Advanced Systems and Robotics' nor 'micro-fulfillment' appears in Walmart EDGAR filings (0 hits each). The 400-unit purchase commitment is CONTINGENT on satisfaction of defined performance metrics, and as of Sept 27, 2025 SYM is operating only 'several' micro-fulfillment systems with first next-gen prototypes planned for calendar 2026. Walmart's own deal disclosure detail is thin.
moderate_claims.interpretation: MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY. The headline '400-unit + $520M' figure is real-contract but mostly contingent and forward-looking. Calibration Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational) and Heuristic 9 (pilot vs deployment conflation) apply: 'several' operating micro-fulfillment systems vs 400 promised is a wide ladder gap. Walmart's lack of granular EDGAR disclosure of micro-fulfillment / ASR (only the parent name reaches earnings slides) is consistent with the deal being non-material from Walmart's vantage — appropriate for the size of Walmart, but it means the framework cannot independently verify pace of deployment milestones from the counterparty side.

moderate_claims.claim_text: GreenBox JV with SoftBank (SYM 35% / SoftBank 65%): $7.5B 6-year commitment; $11.6B remaining performance obligation at Sept 27, 2025; SYM max exposure $1.57B incl. $1.56B future funding commitments
supports: greenbox_widely_referenced_in_sym_filings
moderate_claims.M_value: 33 EDGAR fulltext hits for 'GreenBox Systems'; all from Symbotic's own filings (no third-party SEC filer corroboration — SoftBank's relevant entity SVF II Strategic Investments AIV LLC and Sunlight Investment Corp are not regular SEC filers). GreenBox commercial agreement and amendments are filed as SYM exhibits. FY25 GreenBox-related revenue recognized: $83.0M (vs $6.0M FY24). Contract liabilities to GreenBox: $142.7M; deferred revenue ramping.
moderate_claims.interpretation: MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY. The JV structure and commitments are real and disclosed, but the $7.5B / $11.6B headline backlog with a 35%-owned VIE that SYM must FUND (max exposure $1.57B) raises Heuristic 11 concerns: the second-largest 'customer' is one in which SYM is a material equity participant and funding source. SoftBank's investment is investment-not-customer-revenue per Heuristic 4. Actual GreenBox revenue ($83M FY25) is only ~1.1% of $7.5B commitment, six years in nominal term but only ~2.5 years actually elapsed since the July 2023 commitment — slow start vs the trajectory required to hit $7.5B by July 2029, with optional 2-year extension. No counterparty side independent SEC corroboration.

moderate_claims.claim_text: C&S Wholesale Grocers is an affiliate / related-party customer; shared executives with SYM; FY revenue from C&S: $12.2M (FY25), $58.9M (FY24), $15.8M (FY23)
supports: cs_wholesale_widely_referenced_in_third_party_filings
moderate_claims.M_value: 339 EDGAR fulltext hits for 'C&S Wholesale' across multiple filers (SpartanNash, Albertsons, Kroger M&A filings, Symbotic DEF 14As). C&S itself is private (no SEC filings of its own), but it is a real, large, frequently-named grocery wholesaler. SYM's revenue from C&S declined sharply from $58.9M FY24 to $12.2M FY25 (-79%), per SYM's own related-party note.
moderate_claims.interpretation: MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY. The relationship is real and corroborated by third-party filings. Concern: (1) related-party customer with shared executives is a governance/conflict flag per the 10-K's own risk factor; (2) the steep FY24→FY25 revenue decline from C&S (-79%) is not highlighted in management discussion but is visible only in the related-party note — suggesting that one of the few non-Walmart commercial customers is rapidly de-scaling. This sharpens, rather than mitigates, the Walmart-concentration risk.

moderate_claims.claim_text: One customer accounted for 22.2% of total revenue in fiscal 2024 (24.0% in 2023, 22.6% in 2022).

moderate_claims.M_value: Amazon (AMZN, CIK 1018724): 7 hits — but all in 2022-2024 context of the now-terminated merger agreement (8-K, 10-Q, 10-K disclosures of the iRobot acquisition deal), NOT customer-relationship disclosure. Walmart (WMT): 0 hits. Target (TGT): 0 hits.
moderate_claims.interpretation: The 22.2% customer is unnamed in iRobot's 10-K (only required to disclose if a single customer >10%; name not required by GAAP). At ~$151M of annual revenue (22.2% of $681.8M), this is material to iRobot but immaterial to any megacap retailer (Amazon retail GMV >$500B, Walmart ~$650B revenue), so the customer would NOT have a counterparty-disclosure obligation under Layer 3 Rule 7. Heuristic 7 second branch applies: 'ABSENCE for a relationship where the customer has no recognition obligation' = no contradiction. However, the company is NOT naming the customer despite multi-year >20% concentration, which is a moderate-weight disclosure-completeness concern given the Amazon-merger backdrop (the 22% customer could plausibly be Amazon retail). Score MODERATE.
